root_cause.text: The xfrm_policy_fini() function fails to synchronize the policy_hthresh.work work item during namespace teardown, allowing queued work callbacks to execute after the struct net has been freed and access stale memory via container_of().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `disable_work_sync(&net->xfrm.policy_hthresh.work);` to xfrm_policy_fini() before the existing `flush_work(&net->xfrm.policy_hash_work);` call. The CVE description explicitly states that "xfrm_policy_fini() already flushes policy_hash_work during teardown, but it does not synchronize policy_hthresh.work," and that the xfrm_hash_rebuild() callback "retrieves the enclosing struct net via container_of()" which will dereference freed memory if the work outlives namespace teardown. The fix ensures policy_hthresh.work cannot be queued or running after the net namespace begins teardown.

intent_record.how: This change ensures that the policy hash threshold work queue is disabled and synchronized before flushing the policy hash work queue. This prevents potential race conditions where the threshold work might be scheduled or executing while cleanup is in progress, ensuring orderly shutdown of work queue handlers.
